# Eval arena wrap parity

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC5.

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want the headless eval arena to mirror the shipped
wrap-around world, so wrap-aware play actually earns eval credit and eval scores
measure the same physics the bot faces in the game.

## Context

The headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) diverges from the game in two ways:

- **Bullets are culled off-field** — `offField(point, width, height)` with
  `BULLET_MARGIN` retires player and enemy bullets once they leave the playfield,
  whereas the game wraps both (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`, four-edge
  wrap, AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0).
- **Hostile fire aims at the raw player position** — the enemy bullet is launched
  with `dx = player.x - hostile.x` on the raw line, so no hostile shot ever
  crosses a seam, even though wrap-aware enemies now fire along the shortest
  wrapped path.

Consequence: a wrap-aware bot is scored in a world where the seam does not exist
for bullets, so the epic's behaviour earns no credit and eval-driven tuning is
misleading.

## Scope

1. Wrap player and enemy bullets at the four edges each tick (position-only
   modulo on the playfield period, matching
   `src/utils/movementModel.ts`/`bulletLifecycle.ts`), retiring the off-field
   cull for bullets that are alive by lifetime. Bullet lifetime/expiry semantics
   are preserved.
2. Aim hostile fire along the shortest wrapped path using the shared seam maths
   (`aimVectorToTarget`, `wrapAware: true`) so eval hostile fire matches the
   wrap-aware enemy fire in the game — no copy of the aim maths in
   `src/ai/eval/`.
3. Keep everything else about the arena unchanged (drops, minerals, hit radii,
   metrics), so scores stay comparable; document the parity change in
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` (the fuller docs pass lives in the docs child, but this
   note is required here).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is at wrap-parity with the
   game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of being culled off-field, and
   player bullets do too (matching the game's bullet wrap model), while bullet
   lifetime expiry is preserved.
2. Hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped path (shared
   `aimVectorToTarget`/wrapped-delta maths, no duplicate implementation), so an
   enemy near one edge fires at a player near the opposite edge across the seam.
3. `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet case (a bullet crossing
   each edge reappears on the opposite side and is not culled) and the seam-aim
   case (a hostile's launched bullet heading equals the wrapped-path heading),
   plus a regression case proving a same-side shot is unchanged.
4. Eval metrics capture wrap-aware play: a test (or the existing metric
   assertions) shows a bullet that crossed the seam is still counted as a
   live/hittable projectile rather than being retired, so avoidable-hit and
   damage metrics are computed on the wrapped world.
5. `docs/EVALUATION.md` documents the wrap parity (bullets wrap, hostile fire is
   seam-aware) and any metric interpretation change.
6. The full eval suite (`src/ai/eval/*.test.ts`) stays green and the changed-scope
   test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit order) with tests
   written first.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — bullet stepping/retirement, hostile fire launch.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — wrapped-bullet and seam-aim cases (written first).
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — wrap-parity note.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the wrap-geometry primitives child and the seam-aware aim child
(shared wrapped aim maths).

As a **developer**, I want the bot framework and evaluation docs to describe the

   preserved human-like governor (reaction cadence, W/A/D, thrust feel).

## Problem

AC5 requires every real divergence found by the sweep to be fixed **with a regression test**. D3 (spawner-delivered archetypes/hazards missing from GymLevel) was fixed by AH-0MVRMHWNC002H4B5 through the shared `src/scenes/core/dynamicSpawnPlan.ts` planner/release seam, and `src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts` proves cross-scene parity for **four** of the five delivered archetypes — centipede, ghosts, horde and lane traffic (`describe('GymLevel × PlayScene — spawner-delivered content parity (D3)')`, cases list at ~:944).

The fifth, **telegraphed orbital strikes** (`StrikeSpawner` → `planStrikeWaveSpawns` / `_spawnScheduledStrike`), has no cross-scene parity case. It is covered only by `src/waves/StrikeSpawner.test.ts` (pure planner) and the `releaseDueSpawns` unit tests in `src/scenes/core/dynamicSpawnPlan.test.ts`, so the matrix wording 'pinned by src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts (D2, D3)' overstates the parity coverage for strikes. The fresh audit of AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV records AC5 as `partial` on exactly this point.

## Why it was omitted

`planStrikeWaveSpawns` returns no strikes before `STRIKE_SPAWN_START_WAVE` (3) — it takes `globalWaveIndex` — while the D3 parity harness (`dynamicProbe(flag)` at ~:871) boots a single-wave level, so the plan is empty. A strike case needs the harness to advance the launched level to its third wave (or to seed `globalWaveIndex`) before comparing plans.

1. Extend `dynamicProbe` (or add a sibling probe) so the strike case reaches `globalWaveIndex >= 3` — advance the level through two waves (preferred: drive the real wave-complete path) or expose a test-only seam for the global wave index; no production behaviour change.
2. Extend `plannedDynamic` with an `orbitalStrike` branch reading `pendingStrikeSpawns` and add a fifth case to the D3 cases list with `count: (scene) => scene.strikesSpawnedThisWave`, asserting (a) both scenes plan a non-zero, equal strike count and (b) both release equal counts over an identical dt sequence.
3. Keep the existing four cases unchanged and green.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts` D3 suite contains an orbital-strike case asserting equal non-zero planned counts in `GymLevel` and `PlayScene` for the same level/wave definition.

- `src/scenes/core/dynamicSpawnPlan.ts` (`planStrikeWaveSpawns`, `releaseDueSpawns`)

- Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC5).
- Fix that introduced the shared seam: AH-0MVRMHWNC002H4B5; audit item: AH-0MVRMHUOG005P38A.

## Update 2026-10-29 — use the capture `startWave` seam, and fix the global wave index it exposes

The operator pointed out that a gym scene can be started with a pre-set configuration, so the test does **not** need to play through to wave 3. That works, but only after one prerequisite fix:

- **Capture seam.** \`GymLevel\` already honours \`startWave\` (\`pendingStartWaveIndex\`, re-applied in \`create()\`), and \`PlayScene\` honours dev launch \`startWave\` (\`devStartWave\` → \`WaveManager.beginGame(level, startWave)\`). So both scenes can be started **directly on the strike wave**.

## Goal

As a player, I want an Orbital Strike bolt to land on the **nearest live enemy** — never on an inert asteroid — so the strike reads as a real attack and its damage (1 hit at level 1) is never wasted chipping a rock.

## Parent

AH-0MVRE6N08001TE4V — Orbital Strike does nothing (accepted criteria AC1/AC3; producer manual rejection 2026-10-29T15:58Z).

## Producer rejection (source of this item)

The parent's audit record (`wl audit-show AH-0MVRE6N08001TE4V`) carries a manual rejection from the producer:

> Rejected by manual review. This is still firing too slowly, I thought we agreed it would fire approx every 7s. We should also stop it fitting on asteroids, we want it to fire on the nearest enemy

Two clauses must be closed:

1. **Targeting.** The bolt must ignore asteroids and strike the nearest enemy.
2. **Cadence.** The permanent strike must fire roughly every 7 s. The shipped dev cadence after commit `4c69634f` is a whole-beat cadence on the shared 80 BPM grid: **9 beats = 6.75 s** from the first grant, −1 beat per level, floored at 3 beats (2.25 s). Registry-level tests exist (`src/powerups/effects.test.ts`), but nothing pins the cadence **end-to-end through the real shared step** (`CombatCoreScene._updateOrbitalStrike`) that the game and every gym actually run, so a regression there would be invisible. This item adds that end-to-end evidence and records the measured value on the parent so the producer can confirm they are playing a build that includes `4c69634f`.

## Context (research)

- `CombatScene.onOrbitalStrike` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:642`) picks the nearest live entity from `getEnemyEntities()` with no archetype filter.
- `PlayScene.getEnemyEntities()` returns `this.spawned.map((s) => s.entity)` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3702`), and asteroids are pushed into `spawned` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1934` `_spawnScheduledAsteroid`, `:4839` `spawnAsteroidAt`) with `enemyKey: 'asteroid'`. Asteroids are non-blocking world hazards, not enemies (`src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts:77`, `miniBossDeathSweep` classify `asteroid` and `lane-traffic` as hazards).
- Every enemy entity exposes `archetype` (`BaseEnemy.archetype`, defaults to `'unknown'`; `Asteroid.archetype === 'asteroid'`), which is how `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts:375` already separates asteroids by archetype.
- Therefore a bolt can currently pick a rock that happens to be closer than the nearest enemy: the bolt is spent for 1 hull point of rock damage and the player sees no effect — the reported "does nothing" behaviour.

## Deliverables

- New shared helper `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`: the strike's target rule (live, non-asteroid, nearest to the ship) defined **once**, exported for both the game and the gyms. Asteroids are excluded by archetype; entities with no archetype stay targetable so existing stub harnesses and gyms are unaffected.
- `CombatScene.onOrbitalStrike` consumes the helper instead of an inline nearest-entity loop; the damage path (`damageEnemyViaAoe`), the bolt VFX and the cue are unchanged.
- Tests: a unit suite for the helper (nearest wins; a nearer asteroid is skipped; an all-asteroid field yields no target; dead entities are skipped) and shared-core regression tests in `src/scenes/core/orbitalStrikeRetention.test.ts` proving (a) with an asteroid nearer than an enemy the **enemy** takes the bolt and the asteroid takes none, and (b) an asteroid-only field leaves the bolt latched (retained, never wasted on rock) until a real enemy appears.
- An end-to-end cadence test driving the real shared step at 60 Hz for a permanent strike and asserting the bolt lands every 9 beats (6.75 s, the producer's ~7 s) — not just the resolved constant.
- Docs: the GDD §4.4.3 strike paragraph states the asteroid exclusion and the cadence evidence; JSDoc on `onOrbitalStrike` and the new helper records the parent item and the producer's rejection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Nearest enemy, never an asteroid.** `CombatScene.onOrbitalStrike` selects the nearest live enemy whose archetype is not `asteroid`; a nearer asteroid is never damaged by a strike, asserted by a shared-core test that places the asteroid closer than the enemy.
- **Retention still holds.** When the only live entities are asteroids the bolt stays latched (no silent waste, no volley) and lands on the first real enemy to appear, asserted by a shared-core test.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The targeting rule lives once in `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by the shared strike step, so `PlayScene` and every gym inherit it with no scene-specific copy; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stays green.
- **Cadence evidence, end-to-end.** A test drives `CombatCoreScene._updateOrbitalStrike` at 60 Hz through the real `onOrbitalStrike` and asserts the permanent strike lands every 9 beats (6.75 s ± 1 frame), i.e. the producer's ~7 s, and the measured value is recorded on the parent work item.
- **Docs updated.** GDD §4.4.3 (and the strike JSDoc) describe the asteroid exclusion; docs assertions stay green.
- **No non-strike regressions.** Smart Bomb / Bomb nova rings and the Missile-Command `orbital-strike` hazard are untouched; `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes.

## Constraints

- Cosmetic/targeting scope only: do not change strike damage, the interval values, the drop weight, or the bolt VFX/SFX.
- Do not fork the behaviour into a gym: the rule must stay in the shared core.
- Do not change asteroid behaviour elsewhere (Smart Bomb, bullets, collisions may still hit asteroids).
- Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Parent AC traceability

- Parent AC1 (distinct visual identity) / AC3 (no silent waste) remain satisfied; this item narrows *what* the bolt may land on.
- Parent AC5 (gym↔game parity) is preserved by keeping the rule in the shared core.

**Key Files:**
- src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts
- src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.test.ts
- src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts
- src/scenes/core/orbitalStrikeRetention.test.ts
- docs/Game Design Document.md
- src/vfx/orbitalStrike.docs.test.ts
